items.informal_name: Evaluation Identity (Eta Conversion) for Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] (p : MvPolynomial σ R),
  MvPolynomial.eval₂ MvPolynomial.C MvPolynomial.X p = p
items.informal_description: For any multivariate polynomial $ p $ in variables $ \sigma $ with coefficients in a commutative semiring $ R $, evaluating $ p $ using the constant polynomial embedding $ C : R \to R[\sigma] $ and identity variable mapping $ X : \sigma \to R[\sigma] $ yields the original polynomial $ p $. Symbolically, $ \text{eval}_2(C, X)(p) = p $. This expresses that the canonical evaluation map is the identity when coefficients are embedded as constants and variables are mapped to themselves.

items.informal_name: Diagonal Matrix of Indeterminate X Maps to X under Matrix-Polynomial Equivalence
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] {n : Type w} [inst_1 : DecidableEq n] [inst_2 : Fintype n],
  matPolyEquiv (Matrix.diagonal fun x => Polynomial.X) = Polynomial.X
items.informal_description: The canonical $ R $-algebra isomorphism between $ n 	imes n $ matrices over the polynomial ring $ R[X] $ and polynomials over $ n 	imes n $ matrices with coefficients in $ R $ sends the diagonal matrix with $ X $ on its diagonal to the indeterminate $ X $ itself, i.e., $ \text{matPolyEquiv}(\text{diag}(X,\ldots,X)) = X $. This identifies scalar matrices with constant polynomial coefficients under the isomorphism.

items.informal_name: Expansion Homomorphism for Exponent One is Identity
items.type: ∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R], MvPolynomial.expand 1 = AlgHom.id R (MvPolynomial σ R)
items.informal_description: The expansion homomorphism that substitutes each variable $X_i$ in the multivariate polynomial ring $R[\sigma]$ with $X_i^1$ (i.e., itself) is equal to the identity algebra homomorphism on $R[\sigma]$.

items.informal_name: Variable Substitution Identity in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : σ → MvPolynomial τ R) (i : σ),
  (MvPolynomial.bind₁ f) (MvPolynomial.X i) = f i
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ R $, types $ \sigma $ and $ \tau $, and a function $ f : \sigma \to R[\tau] $, applying the substitution homomorphism $ \text{bind}_1(f) $ to the variable $ X_i \in R[\sigma] $ yields $ f(i) $. In symbols, $ \text{bind}_1(f)(X_i) = f(i) $.

items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R],
  MvPolynomial.bind₁ MvPolynomial.X = AlgHom.id R (MvPolynomial σ R)
items.informal_description: Substituting each variable in the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[\sigma] $ with itself results in the identity algebra homomorphism. That is, the variable substitution homomorphism induced by the identity map $ X : \sigma \to R[\sigma] $ is equal to the identity function on $ R[\sigma] $.

items.informal_name: Algebra Equivalence for Multivariate Polynomials with Incremented Index Type
items.type:
∀ (R : Type u) [inst : CommSemiring R] (n : ℕ) (p : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R),
  (MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv R n) p =
    (MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom (Polynomial.C.comp MvPolynomial.C) fun i =>
        Fin.cases Polynomial.X (fun k => Polynomial.C (MvPolynomial.X k)) i)
      p
items.informal_description: There is an algebra equivalence between the ring of multivariate polynomials over $ \text{Fin}(n+1) $ with coefficients in a commutative semiring $ R $, and the polynomial ring in one variable whose coefficients are multivariate polynomials over $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \text{Fin}(n) $. This equivalence is constructed via the bijection $ \text{Fin}(n+1) \simeq \text{Option}(\text{Fin}(n)) $, mapping the $ \text{none} $ case to the outer polynomial indeterminate and $ \text{some } k $ cases to inner variables. The equivalence preserves addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication by elements of $ R $.

items.type: ∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R], MvPolynomial.bind₁ id = MvPolynomial.join₁
items.informal_description: Applying the variable substitution homomorphism with the identity map on multivariate polynomials $ R[\sigma] $ is equivalent to the flattening homomorphism that reduces nested polynomial structures to a single polynomial layer.

items.informal_name: Univariate Embedding Equals Rename Composition in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {σ : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] (i : σ),
  Polynomial.toMvPolynomial i = (MvPolynomial.rename fun x => i).comp ↑(MvPolynomial.pUnitAlgEquiv R).symm
items.informal_description: The algebra homomorphism embedding a univariate polynomial ring $ R[X] $ into the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[\sigma] $ by substituting $ X $ with the $ i $-th variable in $ \sigma $ is equal to the composition of the inverse of the algebra equivalence between $ R[\mathsf{PUnit}] $ and $ R[X] $ with the renaming of variables from $ \mathsf{PUnit} $ to the $ i $-th variable in $ \sigma $.
